description: Silent Legacy is a solo team in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge under the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" track. We transform real NASA mission archives into an interactive digital storybook for students aged 8–14. Spotlighting retired heroes like Apollo 11's Eagle, Opportunity, Spirit, and Ingenuity, we show what these silent pioneers achieved on the Moon and Mars and how they inspire future Artemis explorers.
summary: Silent Legacy is an interactive storybook that turns NASA’s retired hardware into tales for students aged 8 to 14. Visitors switch between the Moon and Mars, tap glowing pins on an illustrated surface map, and meet six machines: Apollo 11’s Eagle, the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, and the Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and Ingenuity missions. Each profile gives real dates, landing coordinates, the mission’s purpose, and its key discoveries, followed by a short first-person “final transmission” written in plain, friendly language. A five-question quiz rewards players with a downloadable Explorer Badge. The app runs in any browser with no sign-in. It matters because dense mission archives become stories that children remember, and it shows how past pioneers prepare the way for Artemis explorers.
details: Silent Legacy is a single-page web app built with HTML5, Tailwind CSS and vanilla JavaScript. It needs no backend or API keys, so it loads instantly on a school computer or a phone. A Moon/Mars toggle redraws an illustrated surface map with clickable pins. Selecting a pin opens a profile card with mission dates, site coordinates, original purpose, discoveries, and a diary entry told from the machine’s point of view. A Web Audio synth gives optional sound feedback, and the layout adapts to small screens. The Junior Space Historian Quiz has five questions and generates a personalized badge image on a canvas. All facts come from NASA mission pages and archives. The diaries are imagined voices, clearly labeled as such, so that children engage emotionally while the science stays accurate. We considered reading level, accessibility (large tap targets, high contrast, keyboard-friendly buttons), and the idea that “abandoned” does not mean “forgotten.”
